_doc: Devices and firing times for the dashboard v1 recurring job (docs/dashboard-recurring-job-v1.md). scripts/dashboard_job.py reads this; nothing here is a measurement. Paths under hold/hold_cli are the sibling conversion lane's device-hold protocol on the bench host (docs/OPERATIONS.md, 'A phone is shared with other lanes').
_slots_doc: launchd runs `./bench dashboard-job auto` at these local times every night (the plist template carries the same times). `auto` measures, among the devices with no admitted dashboard session since Monday 00:00 local, the attached unheld one whose last admitted session is oldest — the iPhone only inside its auto_window after auto_idle_hours without a record, the Mac only while no heavy export pipeline runs. One device per firing; each device once a week (a device whose set is in `parts`, the Mac: once per part, one part per firing); a firing with nothing pending exits 0. A Developer Device Platform lab unit (platform ddp) is not the firing's device: no device on this host, so its weekly sitting runs after the firing's attached-device sitting (or at a firing with none), docs/dashboard-autopilot-v1.md section 9. A device whose entry says `auto`: false is never chosen by `auto` (its report line reads by-hand): it is measured only by `./bench dashboard-job <key>`, by hand, in a window the owner offers.

m4max.window: any firing while no heavy export pipeline runs (unified-memory contention: the runner refuses and the job passes over the Mac until it is quiet)
m4max._parts_doc: The Mac's weekly set as two sittings on two firings, one part each, in this order: part b (Qwen3 4B, Gemma 4 E4B) first, part a (Qwen3 0.6B / 1.7B, Gemma 4 E2B) second, because part a holds the session anchor's model and the page shows a cell's newest session. The whole set (61 cells) outgrew the 5 h timeout: on 2026-10-28 it was cut after 58 cells (24 gate re-runs, 159.5 min of cooldowns), about 5.4 h for all 61. expected_hours per part from the 2026-10-28 m4max log: each cell's span that night (its start to the next cell's cooldown; the last started cell's to the timeout; the three cells the night did not reach from the 2026-10-19 02:00 log), each cell's own cooldown before it in the part's order, and that night's preflight (1.3 min) and anchor phase (7.1 min). timeout_hours is per sitting, 1.6 x the longer part. docs/dashboard-recurring-job-v1.md section 3, 'The Mac set in two parts'

extra_cells._doc: ONNX Runtime GenAI, the two Qwen3 short-chat cells that give valid runs on this phone (owner GO 2026-10-09); runs as its own tagged session (-ort) after the set, whole or halves

llama.cpp on the NPU and the Adreno GPU (side build b11469-snapdragon): the session anchor and the short-chat cells of matrices/dashboard-npu-v1-android-s26.cells (owner GO 2026-10-09; the 1K and protocol cells stay by-hand); its own tagged session (-npu) after the ONNX Runtime one, about 2.1 h; skipped while /data/local/tmp/llmbench/engines/b11469-snapdragon is not on the phone (android/README.md, 'Side builds'). Its five GGUF files are the storage halves' own copies (a: Qwen3 0.6B / 1.7B, Gemma 4 E2B; b1: Qwen3 4B; b2: Gemma 4 E4B), on the phone when it starts; min_free_gb is the room to push back the ones a rotation between the halves can take away (Qwen3 1.7B, Gemma 4 E2B, Qwen3 4B: 6.6 GB as the job counts space, KiB / 10^6, on the phone's models/ listing of 2026-10-08), not its 11.8 GB footprint: a floor above the free space the halves leave (13.9 GB after them on 2026-10-05) would rotate the halves' LiteRT bundles and caches out every week

s26.window: any firing; USB attached, screen on or off (read and stamped per launch); runs unmasked (devices/galaxy-s26.md); the NPU / GPU session needs the llama.cpp side build in /data/local/tmp/llmbench/engines/b11469-snapdragon on the phone

pixel8a.window: any firing; USB attached, screen on or off (read and stamped per launch); storage-limited, so the set runs as three sessions with pushed models rotated out between them

iphone17pro.window: by hand only (auto: false, owner 2026-10-18: the owner's daily phone, not a bench device; the bench iPhone is the 18 Pro). `./bench dashboard-job iphone17pro` inside a window the owner offers, the phone plugged and unlocked (Auto-Lock Never), one hold at a time; a plugged phone in a warm room reports 'fair' (admitted only through the anchor rule). udid is the UDID `devicectl list devices` prints (until 2026-10-18 the entry carried the CoreDevice id, which iphone_attached never matched: docs/dashboard-recurring-job-v1.md section 9)

iphone18pro.window: the 05:30 firing only (auto_window 05:00-08:00 local) and only after 4 h without a record from the phone (auto_idle_hours); the bench iPhone, kept on USB; it must be unlocked (Auto-Lock Never) or the headless launch is refused. udid is the UDID that `devicectl list devices` prints (the job finds the phone there by it); hold is the iPhone lanes' own lockfile (noclobber, a JSON line with a keeper pid or a text line)

s26-ddp.window: any firing, after the attached device's sitting (a lab unit on Google's Developer Device Platform: no device, no hold, no reboot and no anchor phase on this host, so it never takes the firing's one device) or at a firing with none; at most once in interval_days (6): no admitted session of the unit in the last 6 days, and no sitting in them that ran Device Run sessions and was not admitted (a person looks before another is billed); a rolling window, not the Monday week of the attached devices, so a Sunday-night sitting is not repeated by the Monday 02:00 firing. Only while ops/autopilot/switch.json ddp_weekly is true (user 2026-10-16: no per-session GO for DDP; set it false when a Googler runs the weekly DDP set on their side) and the plan's Device Run sessions are within its ddp_max_sessions. identifier = the device string build_summary gives a lab unit's records (the team page's STAND_IN key); the rows run on whichever units of the m1q-36 pool the sessions get (android/ddp/devices.json). expected_hours / timeout_hours: the 2026-10-16 pass ran 12 of these jobs in 151 device-min, the jobs of one session side by side on several units (92 min wall in three streams); the 16 jobs here are 2 sessions, about 3.2 device-hours, longer when the pool has fewer free units
